title: deadline-aware-coalescer: adaptive coalescing windows with KV-affinity preservation
author: Maya Thompson
release_notes: Improves tail latency and throughput by introducing deadline-aware coalescing windows; preserves KV cache hotness to avoid eviction-induced penalty. No API changes.
description:
Context and motivation: Continuous-batching at high concurrency must balance per-request latency SLOs and batch efficiency. Previous batching relied on static coalesce windows and best-effort KV cache locality which led to intermittent p99 regressions under skewed KV access patterns. This PR implements a deadline-aware coalescing scheduler that adapts coalesce windows per-queue based on observed deadline pressure and explicitly preserves KV-cache affinity to avoid degrading the KV hit rate during aggressive coalescing.

Design summary: single-string overview of the approach so it appears as one continuous description. The scheduler introduces three cooperating mechanisms: (1) per-deadline micro-queues: requests are bucketed by remaining time-to-deadline into tight (<5ms), medium (5-25ms), and relaxed (>25ms) lanes to limit cross-impact slowdowns; (2) adaptive coalesce windows: each lane measures recent batching benefit (avg tokens/batch, head-of-line delay) and grows/shrinks its coalesce window using an additive-increase/multiplicative-decrease rule to chase throughput without violating SLOs; (3) KV-affinity preservation: each incoming request annotates the KV-keys it will access (best-effort) and the scheduler will attempt to coalesce requests that touch overlapping key sets into the same batch or hold back non-overlapping requests that would evict hot KV entries. We added soft pin reservations and a short-lived "affinity token" that biases batch composition without hard starvation.

Implementation notes: changes touch scheduler core (scheduler/coalesce.go), KV cache manager (kv/cache_affinity.go), metrics (observability/batching_metrics.prom), and e2e harness (bench/e2e_coalesce_test.go). The adaptive window uses a lightweight ring buffer estimator to track per-lane batch efficiency and a recent-deadline counter to trigger immediate flushes when a lane approaches SLO violation. KV-affinity is implemented as a compact bloom-filter hint per request (opaque to callers) to keep overhead minimal. We added unit tests for the ring estimator and integration tests that simulate heavy KV-skew and mixed workload latencies.

Benchmarks: microbench on a 8xA100 cluster with synthetic chat workload (80% short-turn, 20% long-turn) and KV-skew (top-20 keys hot): compared to main at time of PR the changes show: median latency +2% (tradeoff for throughput), p95 -8%, p99 -12%, sustained throughput +11% when coalescing windows adapt; KV hit-rate +6 percentage points in hot-key scenarios, which explains the tail latency improvement. Under uniform key access there is no regression in KV hit-rate.

Testing and CI: local unit test coverage added for estimator and KV hints. Integration bench harness included as a fast smoke test in CI; full cluster perf runs were done offline and results archived in the PR thread (link to internal benchmark page). CI initially failed on a race in the affinity token lifetime; fixed by moving token cleanup to the scheduler event loop and adding a deterministic clock in tests. Final CI status: pass.

Rollout and safety: feature gated behind a runtime flag (env REDWOOD_COALESCE_V2) and default-off for Dedicated customers until canary confirms improvements. Automatic fallback: when the adaptive window detects sustained SLO violations for a lane, it disables coalescing for that lane for a cooldown period. We also added tracing spans for diagnostics: scheduler.coalesce.window and scheduler.kv.affinity.

Checklist: - [x] design doc linked (ENG-9481) - [x] unit tests - [x] integration bench harness - [x] docs: console metrics added - [x] gated rollout flag - [x] changelog entry prepared

Related work: builds on ENG-8622 continuous-batching refactor and references prior fairness work but focuses on deadline-sensitive coalescing and KV-preservation rather than queue-prioritization.
